subject: Geopolitics
title: Fragility in the 21st Century
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fragility in the 21st Century.

hook.text: 1.8 billion people live in fragile states today. By 2030, that number could reach 2.3 billion. The trend is worsening.

buildup.text: Climate change, population growth, and rising inequality are stacking pressure on the world's weakest states.

discovery.text: COVID-19 pushed dozens of countries deeper into fragility. Pandemics hit hardest where systems are already broken.

twist.text: Technology can help: mobile banking, satellite monitoring, digital governance.

climax.text: Fragility is the defining challenge of this century.

punchline.text: Fragile states are not a distant problem. They are everyone's problem.

quiz.question: Why is state fragility a growing global concern?
options: The number of countries in the world is increasing
Climate change, inequality, and pandemics intensify existing weaknesses
Fragile states are gaining nuclear weapons
